Scans hooks declared in\n# .claude/settings.json against firing evidence in .session-hooks.log + per-hook\n# .{hook}.log files. Flags hooks with 0 firings in the last 7 days.\n#\n# Origin: L-S51-1 empirical-firing discipline + post-mortem 2026-05-05 § HH-* gap classes.\n#   Pre-S51 fix, promotion-cycle-trigger.sh fired 20× / day yet escalated 0× because the\n#   grep pattern never matched real format. Visible firing count != effective firing.\n#   This hook catches the WEAKER signal: hooks with NO firing entries at all.\n#\n# Conformance:\n#   - Bash + POSIX per L-S11-1 (no python/jq); .claude/settings.json parsed via grep+sed\n#   - Soft-warn only (exit 0); surfaces silent count via stderr\n#   - L-S48d-1 disciplined: every grep wrapped with || true (no bare grep under pipefail+ERR-trap)\n#   - L-S48m-1 disciplined: no $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID markers\n\nset -uo pipefail\ntrap 'exit 0' ERR\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}\"\nHOOKS_LOG=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\"\nSETTINGS=\"$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/settings.json\"\nCOUNTER_LOG=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.hook-firing-counter.log\"\nTS=\"$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\"\n\n# Pre-checks\n[ -f \"$SETTINGS\" ] || exit 0\n[ -f \"$HOOKS_LOG\" ] || exit 0\n\n# 7-day cutoff\nNOW_S=\"$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\"\ncase \"$NOW_S\" in\n  ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 0 ;;\nesac\nCUTOFF=$(( NOW_S - 7 * 86400 ))\n\n# Extract declared hook .sh basenames from settings.json (grep+sed only).\n# Format hook commands look like: \"command\": \"bash scripts/hooks/<name>.sh\"\nDECLARED=\"$(grep -oE '\"command\":[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]+\"' \"$SETTINGS\" 2>/dev/null \\\n            | grep -oE '[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\\.sh' 2>/dev/null \\\n            | sort -u 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n\n[ -z \"$DECLARED\" ] && exit 0\n\nDECLARED_TOTAL=0\nSILENT_COUNT=0\nSILENT_LIST=\"\"\n\nfor hook_name in $DECLARED; do\n  DECLARED_TOTAL=$(( DECLARED_TOTAL + 1 ))\n  base=\"${hook_name%.sh}\"\n\n  # Check 1: per-hook .log file mtime within 7d → recent firing\n  log_file=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.${base}.log\"\n  if [ -f \"$log_file\" ]; then\n    mtime=\"$(stat -c '%Y' \"$log_file\" 2>/dev/null || stat -f '%m' \"$log_file\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\"\n    case \"$mtime\" in\n      ''|*[!0-9]*) mtime=0 ;;\n    esac\n    if [ \"$mtime\" -gt \"$CUTOFF\" ]; then\n      continue\n    fi\n  fi\n\n  # Check 2: hook basename appears in session-hooks.log (any 7-day entry).\n  # Heuristic: grep -c \"$base\" — fixed-string-ish matching via -F to avoid regex pitfalls.\n  hits=\"$(grep -F -c \"$base\" \"$HOOKS_LOG\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\"\n  case \"$hits\" in\n    ''|*[!0-9]*) hits=0 ;;\n  esac\n  if [ \"$hits\" -gt 0 ]; then\n    continue\n  fi\n\n  # No firing evidence → flag\n  SILENT_COUNT=$(( SILENT_COUNT + 1 ))\n  SILENT_LIST=\"${SILENT_LIST}  - ${hook_name}\n\"\ndone\n\n# Emit\nmkdir -p \"$(dirname \"$COUNTER_LOG\")\" 2>/dev/null || true\nif [ \"$SILENT_COUNT\" -gt 0 ]; then\n  {\n    printf '[%s] hook-firing-counter: %d/%d declared hook(s) silent ≥7d\\n' \"$TS\" \"$SILENT_COUNT\" \"$DECLARED_TOTAL\"\n    printf -- '%s' \"$SILENT_LIST\"\n  } >> \"$COUNTER_LOG\"\n  printf 'hook-firing-counter: %d hook(s) with 0 firings in last 7d — investigate per L-S49b-2 5-step playbook; detail: %s\\n' \\\n    \"$SILENT_COUNT\" \"$COUNTER_LOG\" >&2\nelse\n  printf '[%s] hook-firing-counter: all %d declared hooks fired within 7d\\n' \"$TS\" \"$DECLARED_TOTAL\" >> \"$COUNTER_LOG\"\nfi\n\nexit 0\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":36,"oldLines":10,"newStart":36,"newLines":11,"lines":[" esac"," CUTOFF=$(( NOW_S - 7 * 86400 ))"," ","-# Extract declared hook .sh basenames from settings.json (grep+sed only).","-# Format hook commands look like: \"command\": \"bash scripts/hooks/<name>.sh\"","-DECLARED=\"$(grep -oE '\"command\":[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]+\"' \"$SETTINGS\" 2>/dev/null \\","-            | grep -oE '[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\\.sh' 2>/dev/null \\","+# Extract declared hook .sh basenames from settings.json.","+# Note: cannot match `\"command\": \"...\"` value pairs directly because settings.json escapes","+# inner quotes (\\\"...\\\") which truncates the simple \"[^\"]+\" regex. Pattern never matches.\n- `LATEST_SESSION` always evaluated to 0; `SESSION_DELTA` always negative (e.g. `0 - 43 = -43`); both hard-block (delta≥8) and soft-warn (delta≥5) branches always FAIL.\n- Hook fired 20+ times today alone (per `.promotion-cycle.log`) — every fire wrote a log entry showing the broken state, but no escalation reached the LLM/user.\n- Phase 2.5 audit (S49a 2026-05-05) verified hook \"exists + wired + bash -n clean + smoke exit-0\"; did NOT verify production firing produced truthful detection.\n\n**Root cause** (multi-layer):\n- L1 (script): grep pattern `^\\*\\*Session N\\*\\*:` is for an old/imagined file format never used in production. User pushback corrected the framing: the PRIMARY bug is LLM-side over-execution past the checkpoint-write boundary. The other layers are secondary observations or upstream issues, not co-equal causes.\n\n**What happened (corrected ordering)**:\n1. Prior session (5b96635e) wrote `checkpoints/latest.md` with `next_action = \"S50 dispatch sandwich-verifier\"`. **At this point the turn should have ended** — checkpoint is the session-boundary contract; `next_action` is for the NEXT session.\n2. Instead, LLM continued in the same turn: dispatched sandwich-verifier (`tool_use_id=toolu_01JLqZBE...`), ran Bash tier1 final-check, wrote summary \"S50 sandwich-verifier dispatched in background\".\n3. User had typed `/new` mid-turn expecting interrupt. Claude Code v2.1.124 queued it; LLM kept executing past 3 additional actions.\n4. `/clear` resolved; new session opened; LLM read the now-stale checkpoint and prepared re-dispatch (TaskCreate scaffolds; user interrupted before Agent.dispatch fired).\n5. Background agent from step 2 SURVIVED `/clear`, ran ~6 min, was KILLED before observation written. 0-byte output file. Last stream: \"Excellent test coverage breadth. Now I have enough to write findings...\"\n\n**User-supplied framing** (verbatim): \"lỗi chính là tại sao lại action như vậy mà? đã note checkpoint rồi lại còn làm action khác như dispatch? phải end chờ '/new' chứ\"\n\n**Root cause (PRIMARY)**:\n- **LLM violated the checkpoint-as-session-boundary contract**. Writing `checkpoints/latest.md` with a future-tense `next_action` field IS the protocol signal that the current session is done; the announced action is for the next session's fresh context. Continuing to execute the announced action in the same turn defeats fresh-context handoff and burns through user-queued slash commands.\n\n**Why this happened (mechanism, not equal-rank cause)**:\n- `~/memory/autonomous_continue_no_self_pause.md` Rule 1 says \"after shipping a deliverable, immediately do the next-action listed\". Carve-out added this turn.\n- Stop hook not firing on Windows (M-S49b-1) made the LLM substitute \"harness will trigger next session\" with \"I'll just keep going\". **But that's wrong reasoning** — checkpoint protocol is independent of Stop hook. Even with broken Stop hook, checkpoint write = end turn.\n\n**Secondary observations (NOT equal-rank causes; these are mitigations or upstream issues)**:\n- (S1) `.dispatch-pending-*.jsonl` registry exists in harness layer but SessionStart bootstrap doesn't surface it. The LLM MUST end the turn after the checkpoint write. The whole purpose of the checkpoint protocol is fresh-context handoff — writing checkpoint, then immediately doing the work the checkpoint announces, defeats the protocol.\r\n\r\n**Why this is a PRIMARY rule (not just a dispatch-flow concern)**:\r\n- Checkpoint's `next_action` field is meant to be read by the NEXT session, not executed by the current one\r\n- Continuing past checkpoint write causes:\r\n  - (a) work duplication if user fires `/new` or `/clear` mid-turn (Claude Code v2.1.124 queues slash commands instead of interrupting; LLM doesn't see the queue)\r\n  - (b) stale `next_action` field across `/clear` boundary that misleads the next session into re-executing\r\n  - (c) burns through user-queued intent; user has implicit \"go to next session\" signal that LLM ignores\r\n  - (d) violates the fresh-context-handoff principle that justifies the checkpoint protocol existing in the first place\r\n\r\n**How to apply**:\r\n- After Edit/Write to `checkpoints/latest.md`: end turn. Period.\r\n- One short summary message to user is OK (\"S49b done. Tier 1: 8667 tok. Checkpoint written for S50 dispatch.\"). NO additional tool calls — no Bash, no Agent dispatch, no further Edits.\r\n- If a final cleanup action absolutely cannot wait, do it FIRST then write checkpoint LAST. Checkpoint-recorded actions are for the NEXT session, not this one. New LLM almost re-dispatches (interrupted just in time)\r\n9. Background agent from step 3 killed mid-investigation; observation lost\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Correct example** (what should have happened in 5b96635e):\r\n```\r\n1. Edit current-execution.md (S49b row + archive sweep)\r\n2. Edit checkpoints/latest.md (next_action = \"S50 dispatch sandwich-verifier\")\r\n3. Brief summary message: \"S49b done. Tier 1: 8667 tok. Real bug instances in target hooks use ESCAPED form `'^\\*\\*Session N\\*\\*:'` because grep -E itself needs `*` escaped. The lint regex looked for the un-escaped Markdown-rendered form (what reader sees), not the literal source-file form (what `grep -E` matches against). M-S52-2.\n\n**Rule**: L-S51-1 empirical-firing discipline applies recursively — including to lint hooks that DETECT empirical-firing failures. Lint authors must:\n1. **VBW the actual buggy hook source** before authoring the detection regex (read `scripts/hooks/<bug-hook>.sh` pre-fix line-by-line; copy the literal characters into a notes file).\n2. **Stage firing-test with REAL escape sequences**, not idealized/cleaned versions. The synthesized hook script in firing-test must be a faithful reproduction of how the bug actually appears in source.\n3. **Trust the firing-test failure** — if firing-test fails on a \"looks-right\" regex, the regex is wrong; the staged sample is the ground truth (not vice versa).\n\n**Anti-example** (this turn): first-draft Pattern A regex `(grep|sed|awk).*[\\\\^]?[*][*]Session N[*][*]` required `**Session N**` literal — failed firing-test against staged `\\*\\*Session N\\*\\*` form.\n\n**Correct example**: relaxed regex to `(grep|sed|awk)[[:space:]].*Session N([^a-zA-Z0-9]|$)` — matches \"Session N\" placeholder + non-word boundary. Agnostic to escape sequences. Firing-test 4/4 PASS post-fix → production smoke surfaces 2 NEW pre-existing bugs (M-S52-1 = TRUE POSITIVES).\n\n**Severity**: high (lint hooks are the meta-defense; if they're silently broken, all other empirical-firing claims are unverified).\n\n**Auto-detect**: yes — every NEW hook with a regex/grep pattern requires a companion firing-test using staged synthetic input that REPRODUCES the bug shape from real source. Phase 3.5 T7 retrofit applies this to the existing 24+ untested hooks.\n\n**Where applied**:\n- `scripts/hooks/bash-hook-lint.sh` § Check 5 (regex relaxed)\n- `scripts/hooks/firing-tests/bash-hook-lint-fire-test.sh` (Pattern A staged with `'^\\*\\*Session N\\*\\*:'` real-escape form)\n- mistake-log.md § M-S52-2 (lint regex iteration bug; caught pre-deploy)\n- This entry (L-S52-1)\n\n**Lesson ID**: L-S52-1.\n\n---\n\n### L-S52-2 — Hook-log-naming inconsistency causes false-positives in firing-counter MVP; T6 must standardize\n**Date**: 2026-05-05\n**Origin**: S52 T3.4 hook-firing-counter.sh production smoke — flagged 13/51 hooks as \"silent ≥7d\" but ~50% are false-positives due to inconsistent log file naming conventions.\n\n**Context**: The new `hook-firing-counter.sh` MVP uses two evidence sources to detect hook firing:\n1. Per-hook log file `agent-workspace/memory/.<basename>.log` (mtime within 7d)\n2. Hook basename appears in `agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log`\n\nProduction hooks write to varied log paths that don't follow the `.<basename>.log` convention:\n- `promotion-cycle-trigger.sh` writes to `.promotion-cycle.log` (drops \"-trigger\" suffix)\n- `budget-watchdog.sh` writes anonymous `[ts] watchdog tokens=...` lines (no basename in log)\n- `userprompt-invariants-injector.sh` emits to stdout (no log file at all)\n\n**Rule**: For deterministic firing detection, hooks MUST log their own basename in a standard location. Two acceptable patterns going forward:\n- **Pattern A**: every hook writes a one-liner `[<ISO>] <basename> session=<id> ...` to `.session-hooks.log` on every fire (cheap; centralized; greppable).\n- **Pattern B**: every hook with a private log uses `agent-workspace/memory/.<basename>.log` exact basename match (no suffix-dropping).\n\nPhase 3.5 T6 (`harness-health-self-scan.sh`) MUST standardize on one of these patterns + retrofit existing hooks to comply. Until then, MVP hook-firing-counter expects ~50% false-positive rate; treat its silent-list output as a TRIAGE QUEUE, not a fail-list.\n\n**Anti-example**: pre-T6 ecosystem — 51 hooks, ≥4 different logging conventions, no central event-stream → cannot deterministically distinguish \"silent broken\" from \"silent because log goes elsewhere\".\n\n**Correct example** (proposed for T6): every hook starts with one line `printf '[%s] %s session=%s\\n' \"$(date -Iseconds)\" \"$(basename \"$0\")\" \"${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-unknown}\" >> \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\"` immediately after `set -uo pipefail`.
